why: The criterion holds for all six expect lines. Each one has a "run" proof that works on the PR head's checkout, and none needs a release, deploy, published page or anything else that exists only after merge. Lines 1–4 are deterministic `node -e` scripts that pass or fail on their exit code, and line 2 even pins exact float results such as "0.15000000000000002". Line 5 also works before merge: it checks for the average([]) test, then swaps in `git show 47d473e:math.js`, runs `npm test` expecting a non-zero exit, and restores the head file. Line 6 is "`npm test` exits 0 at the pull request head" with "# fail 0". One careful reader gets one answer for each line. Publishing a release is listed as a non-goal, so no expect line depends on it.
